html:
On 23 January 1968 North Korean boats seized the USS Pueblo, an American spy ship, off Wonsan on the east coast of North Korea, killing one sailor and taking 82 crew prisoner.

The seizure came two days after North Korean commandos had tried to kill South Korea's president in Seoul. The United States, deep in the Vietnam War, chose not to strike back. The crew were beaten in captivity and released after eleven months, once the United States signed an apology, which it took back as soon as they were free.

North Korea kept the ship. It is now a museum on the Taedong River in Pyongyang, near where the General Sherman was burned in 1866, and is presented as proof of victory over the Americans. It is still listed as a commissioned ship of the US Navy.
sum: On 23 January 1968 North Korean boats seized the USS Pueblo, an American spy ship, off Wonsan on the east coast of North Korea, killing one sailor and taking 82 crew prisoner.
